races.name: Scone Palace Jousting Tournament Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Trigg
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with proven form at this distance, Harry Skelton booking significant, 36 days since last run could be perfect spacing
runners_data.spotlight: Did well in bumpers and comfortably off the mark over hurdles at Uttoxeter (2m, good); this is tougher than that winnable race but he's well related and entitled to improve plenty more with racing.

runners_data.name: Saint Cunning
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who raced freely in bumper debut, trainer struggling for winners but could improve significantly over hurdles
runners_data.comment: Killygowan might be the yard first strong but the betting will provide more clues
runners_data.spotlight: Ordinary form when fifth in a bumper here but did go off only 5-1 and he raced freely before weakening late on; could improve on that but clearly needs to.

runners_data.name: Kibris
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with course advantage from recent win here, first tongue-tie applied suggests breathing concerns being addressed
runners_data.comment: Big shout at best but ended time with Joseph O'Brien on a low note
runners_data.spotlight: Useful Flat winner for Joseph O'Brien; 0-4 over hurdles for that yard but came good on stable debut (same ownership) with a narrow win over 2m here last month (good to soft); he would have won easier but for a late mistake; there are some stamina concerns over quite this far.

runners_data.name: Dolly Dior
runners_data.note: Prominent style but insufficient bumper form, 3lb claimer reduces burden but debut over hurdles remains question mark
runners_data.comment: 40-1 and never seriously counted on good ground at Sedgefield earlier this month
runners_data.spotlight: Insufficient promise in two good-ground bumpers to warrant a second look here on hurdle debut.

runners_data.name: Flying Ace
runners_data.note: Recent Cartmel winner carrying momentum, prominent style suits but 11-day turnaround might catch up late on
runners_data.comment: Ran well for a long way on hurdle debut at Downpatrick; probably the one to beat
runners_data.spotlight: Only his second run over hurdles when making no mistake at odds-on in a good-ground 2m1f maiden at Cartmel 11 days ago; the RPR was modest but he did beat a useful Flat recruit and his yard has won three of the last four renewals of this race.

runners_data.name: Busted Springs
runners_data.note: Prominent racer but tailed off in both bumper starts, first-time tongue-tie unlikely to transform poor form
runners_data.comment: Well held on last month's Ayr debut; has a tongue-tie added now
runners_data.spotlight: Tailed off in bumpers at Ayr (heavy) and here (good to soft); huge odds both times.

runners_data.name: Brewdog
runners_data.note: Hold-up style but appalling form record, 300-1 shot behind Kibris here last time tells the story
runners_data.comment: Failed to beat a rival in two bumpers last season; big outsider now hurdling
runners_data.spotlight: 300-1 when tailed off behind Kibris here 24 days ago; no appeal.

races.paceDynamic: Kibris is the clear pace-setter having shown prominent tendencies and local track knowledge from his recent win here. With no other confirmed front-runners in this small field, Kibris will likely dictate terms uncontested through steady fractions over this extended trip. The hold-up horses Trigg and Brewdog will rely on Kibris maintaining a solid gallop to set up their finishing kicks. This controlled pace scenario strongly favours the hold-up merchants who can time their challenges late, particularly over this stamina-testing distance where sustainable pace allows closers to strike.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Kibris sets steady, sustainable fractions without early pressure
scenarios.body: The moderate pace allows hold-up specialists to conserve energy and produce telling late surges. Trigg and other patient rides benefit from the tactical setup over this staying trip.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Kibris maintains his rhythm and kicks when challenged turning for home
scenarios.body: His local course knowledge and recent winning form here gives him tactical advantage to dictate and respond. The prominent racers struggle to reel him in over the extended distance.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Messy Moderate Pace
scenarios.trigger: If the small field and lack of early pace creates a stop-start rhythm
scenarios.body: The uneven tempo disrupts the hold-up horses' timing while not being fast enough to trouble Kibris. Prominent racers benefit from the tactical muddle and positioning advantages.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Unexpected Early Duel
scenarios.trigger: If Flying Ace or Dolly Dior challenge Kibris for the early lead
scenarios.body: The increased pace over this staying trip compromises all three front-runners late on. Hold-up horses benefit from the stronger gallop but face a bigger deficit to make up.

watchPoints.text: Kibris could get loose on the lead if no pressure materializes early, making him very difficult to peg back
Trigg's 36-day break could leave him short of peak fitness despite the Skelton team's strong conditioning
Flying Ace's quick 11-day turnaround from Cartmel may tell in the closing stages over this longer trip
Saint Cunning raced keenly in his bumper so watch for early restraint from McLernon to preserve stamina
Small field dynamics could create tactical complications if the pace collapses completely

races.name: Sun Racing The Home Of Racing Novices' Limited Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Morandi Second
runners_data.note: Long absence of 326 days and poor recent hurdles record makes him hard to trust despite workable mark
runners_data.spotlight: 0-11 over hurdles and absent since weakening fifth at Uttoxeter (2m, good) last summer; current mark is workable but others have more pressing claims.

runners_data.name: Storm The Dug
runners_data.note: Strong hold-up horse who showed clear improvement when second over course and distance on handicap debut
runners_data.spotlight: Fair Flat racer (albeit a maiden) who kept on from the rear for clear second behind Breadalbane Lass over C&D (good) on handicap hurdle debut in April; shortlisted.

runners_data.name: Breadalbane Lass
runners_data.note: Confirmed course winner with proven finishing kick but may struggle off 9lb higher mark than last success
runners_data.comment: Clear winner at Perth last month, her 12th hurdle run; 8lb higher here; still considered
runners_data.spotlight: Kept on too strongy for Storm The Dug over C&D (good) in April, getting off the mark over hurdles at the 12th attempt, but was well held (albeit on soft ground) at Hexham last month; others have more potential.

runners_data.name: Betteryouthanme
runners_data.note: Travelled well for long way on handicap debut and could benefit from drop back to 2m from 2m4f
runners_data.comment: Struggled in three runs in maiden/novice company (huge prices) at Ayr, Wetherby, & Hexham.
runners_data.spotlight: Displayed improvement and travelled well for a long way when third here (2m4f, good to soft) on last month's handicap debut; may benefit from this drop back in trip; one to consider.

runners_data.name: Struth
runners_data.note: Useful flat performer but showed little improvement when fitted with tongue-tie on hurdles debut
runners_data.comment: Useful on Flat in prime but yet to better fair form over hurdles
runners_data.spotlight: Useful on the Flat in his prime but well held when fifth on handicap hurdle debut at Kelso (2m2f, good; first-time tongue-tie) in April and showed no significant improvement in a subsequent C&D maiden; needs to up his game.

runners_data.name: Jack Dempsey
runners_data.note: Pulled up last time over longer trip and needs to prove stamina issues won't recur at this distance
runners_data.comment: 0-7; steps back up in trip for h'cap debut and that should bring about some improvement.
runners_data.spotlight: Returned from break with fairly encouraging run in C&D novice in April but was pulled up in 2m4f handicap here last month and has a fair bit more to prove than some of these.

runners_data.name: Bouboule
runners_data.note: Had wind operation before recent runs which may explain poor form but breeding suggests better possible
runners_data.comment: 17-race maiden; hopes are pinned on wind surgery prompting a major turnaround
runners_data.spotlight: Placed in Musselburgh maiden (1m7f, good to soft) in November but has looked out of sorts over hurdles and on the Flat in recent months (had wind op before latest run); needs to turn a corner.

runners_data.name: Allibaba
runners_data.note: In-form performer with back-to-back wins for new stable and proven good ground specialist
runners_data.comment: Made light of a 538-day absence to win for the first time at Market Rasen 12 days ago.
runners_data.spotlight: Returned from long absence with good-ground wins at Market Rasen and Warwick for new stable last month; should cope if the ground is softer here and might still be on the upgrade; must be considered.

runners_data.name: Blondina
runners_data.note: Basement mark for handicap debut but showed little promise in qualifying runs and tendency to fade late
runners_data.comment: Good 3rd at Musselburgh on first Flat run for the yard; she now has something to build on
runners_data.spotlight: Showed no significant promise in her three qualifying races over hurdles in January-March but makes handicap hurdle debut from a basement mark and returns to this code after winning on the Flat (1m4f; RPR 61) last month; interesting.

runners_data.name: Magic Gloves
runners_data.note: Only prominent runner gives him tactical edge but heavy defeats on final starts last season concerning
runners_data.comment: Tailed off in February but encouraging handicap debut prior to that; not written off
runners_data.spotlight: Promising fourth on handicap debut at Musselburgh (1m7f, soft) in December but suffered heavy defeats on final two starts last season, the latter over C&D, and needs subsequent wind op to have made a big difference.

runners_data.name: Karthala
runners_data.note: Decent third behind Allibaba last time and cheekpieces refitted suggest connections expect improvement
runners_data.comment: Has shown in little in three runs over hurdles; makes his handicap hurdle debut.
runners_data.spotlight: Over 8l behind Alibaba when third at Warwick (2m, good; refitted cheekpieces) last month but that was still a pretty good start to his handicap hurdle career and further progress is possible.

runners_data.name: King Kodiak
runners_data.note: Sometimes clumsy jumper with mixed hurdles record despite recent Carlisle placing
runners_data.comment: Clumsy jumper with very mixed hurdling record; ran big race two starts ago, though
runners_data.spotlight: Placed off 5lb higher at Carlisle (2m3f, good to soft) in April but has very mixed record over hurdles and is sometimes a clumsy jumper; safely held on last two outings; others look much safer.

runners_data.name: Bray Dale
runners_data.note: Struggling veteran now 0-10 over hurdles and 2lb out of weights with visor tried unsuccessfully
runners_data.comment: Arrives here after a couple of heavy defeats and has lots to prove.
runners_data.spotlight: Struggled in Hexham seller last month (first-time visor) and is now 0-10 over hurdles; 2lb out of the weights here; difficult to enthuse over.

races.paceDynamic: Magic Gloves is the only confirmed pace-setter in a field dominated by hold-up horses, giving him a clear tactical advantage to dictate terms without pressure. With 12 of 13 runners showing hold-up tendencies, the pace will be measured early before developing into a sprint finish as the field converges from off the pace. This creates a race where Magic Gloves can control the tempo and potentially steal a march, while the hold-up brigade face the challenge of making up ground in a compressed finish. The race shape strongly favours prominent runners who can track the pace and hold-up horses with genuine acceleration, as they'll benefit from the solid gallop Magic Gloves provides.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Magic Gloves Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Magic Gloves gets an uncontested lead and maintains his jumping rhythm
scenarios.body: He dictates a steady pace that suits his stamina before quickening when it matters, making the hold-up horses' task more difficult. His tactical advantage proves decisive as the field struggles to reel him in from too far back.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes too slow mid-race allowing closer finishers to get competitive
scenarios.body: The race becomes a dash from the final hurdle where horses with the best acceleration thrive. Recent winners Storm The Dug and Breadalbane Lass benefit from their proven finishing kicks.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Allibaba Back-to-Back
scenarios.trigger: If the improving Allibaba produces another forward move following his recent double strike
scenarios.body: His current momentum and good ground form carries him past tiring leaders in the final furlong. The 8-year-old's experience tells as younger rivals falter under pressure.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Breakthrough
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely allowing a forgotten horse to emerge from the pack
scenarios.body: A lightly-raced improver like Karthala or Betteryouthanme capitalizes on the modest pace to deliver a surprise. The handicapper's lenient mark proves crucial as class horses disappoint.

watchPoints.text: Magic Gloves jumping - any early mistakes will compromise his tactical advantage and allow hold-up horses to close the gap
Storm The Dug and Breadalbane Lass positions turning in - both need room to deliver their proven finishing kicks
Allibaba's jumping rhythm - back-to-back winner needs to maintain fluency to complete hat-trick
Early pace development - if too slow it negates Magic Gloves' advantage and sets up sprint finish
Betteryouthanme travels through race - handicap debutant showed promise when staying on over longer trip

races.name: Scone Palace International Horse Trials Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Kinbara Firstdraft
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse switching yards after losing his way, needs the pace to collapse completely to get competitive from the rear
runners_data.comment: Return to hurdles could reignite a spark; possibly a few pounds too high in the handicap.
runners_data.spotlight: Won this two years ago and later added another handicap off this mark; however, he has rather lost his way and now kicks off for a new yard; enjoys good ground.

runners_data.name: Just Dottie
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare with poor recent form including a 22-length beating here, jockey takes 3lb off but hard to fancy
runners_data.comment: Unexposed on the Flat but she may need more of a stamina test than this
runners_data.spotlight: Fourth of six on the Flat last time out and beaten 22l here the time before that; a four-time winner in this discipline but reservations at the minute.

runners_data.name: Scriabin
runners_data.note: Front runner with 0-13 record over hurdles, will ensure strong gallop but has never won over obstacles
runners_data.comment: 12-race maiden over hurdles but placed on three of four runs for this yard, including C&D
runners_data.spotlight: 0-3 on the Flat and 0-13 over hurdles, having had a few chances now in maidens and handicaps; has to raise his game.

runners_data.name: Pure Gold
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who has been well beaten in two runs here since April, may be weighted out of contention now
runners_data.comment: 6lb higher than when winning readily at Hexham (2m) last October; this rates a tough test.
runners_data.spotlight: Progressed well last year but the signs are that she might be a shade high in the weights now after heavy defeats here since April.

runners_data.name: Scots Poet
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner coming off a confidence-boosting win at Kelso on good ground, carries 5lb penalty but proven at this level
runners_data.comment: Won at Sedgefield and backed it up with good Hexham second 15 days ago; not taken lightly
runners_data.spotlight: Exposed multiple winner; he would have found the ground too soft when beaten by King Sacre at Hexham and then dug deep to win at Kelso (2m, good; 5lb lower); entitled to have some say.

runners_data.name: Ravenscraig Castle
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose recent form is concerning with poor runs over hurdles and on the Flat, hard to recommend
runners_data.comment: Ran well over hurdles two starts ago; handy mark on best 2025 Flat form; not ruled out
runners_data.spotlight: Good fourth at Musselburgh in March but tailed off in his last run over hurdles and down the field on the Flat last week; others look more likely.

runners_data.name: Ailt An Chorrain
runners_data.note: Natural front runner switching from blinkers to cheekpieces, 67 days since last run may have freshened him up
runners_data.comment: In the frame on both starts since fitted with blinkers; possibilities
runners_data.spotlight: Record of 2-6 over hurdles, though neither win came in a handicap; only one effort of note in five runs over fences and blinkers are replaced by cheekpieces; the stable probably has brighter prospects with Cosmic Soul.

runners_data.name: Largy Meadow
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who needed stronger pace last time when second over 2m4f here, shorter trip should suit better
runners_data.comment: Bustled up winner at Newcastle (2m4f, good; from 2lb lower) penultimate; PU over C&D since
runners_data.spotlight: Runner-up in the two handicaps he has completed and could have done with a truer pace when chasing home the market leader over 2m4f here last time; he's highly likely to get one here and he's one to consider.

runners_data.name: Cosmic Soul
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who has found his form with hat-trick on good ground, perfectly positioned to track early pace
runners_data.comment: Readily landed the odds over C&D 13 days ago; hiked up 10lb now but still the one to beat
runners_data.spotlight: His hat-trick (2m1f-2m4f; good) has come at a cost mark-wise but it was all very straightforward last time at Sedgefield; something has clicked big time and he could deal with another 6lb.

runners_data.name: Alidam
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with finishing quirk who failed to fire at Sedgefield in cheekpieces, 108 days off track raises questions
runners_data.comment: Ex-French; fair third over 2m on h'cap debut; may do better up in trip with headgear tried
runners_data.spotlight: Ex-French gelding; beaten 6l on handicap debut at Huntingdon (2m, soft) but failed to fire at Sedgefield in the new cheekpieces that are retained; others preferred.

runners_data.name: Mr Lincoln
runners_data.note: Prominent runner placed in last two starts, 0-9 record over hurdles but has been running consistently in defeat
runners_data.comment: Twice placed over hurdles this spring and today's trip may be a good fit in this code
runners_data.spotlight: 0-9 over hurdles but placed in his last two attempts and went very close at Carlisle in March (2m1f, good to soft); Thursday's Flat run when sixth wasn't too shoddy; can go well.

runners_data.name: Tigress Lilly
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare returning from wind surgery but was 50-1 on handicap debut here and ran accordingly
runners_data.comment: Not obviously well treated off this opening mark but things may click at some point
runners_data.spotlight: In a good yard and returns from wind surgery, but she was 50-1 for her handicap debut here in April and performed accordingly.

runners_data.name: King Sacre
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who beat Scots Poet by 17 lengths at Hexham, raised 9lb but proven race winner with strong finishing kick
runners_data.comment: Unexposed; improved form when second on h'cap debut at Sedgefield last time; a possible
runners_data.spotlight: Runner-up in his first handicap (on good) and then made all the running on soft ground at Hexham, beating Scots Poet by some 17l; raised 9lb for that but he's far from exposed.

races.paceDynamic: Ailt An Chorrain and Scriabin will contest the early lead, with both confirmed front runners likely to set a genuine gallop over this sharp 2m trip. Cosmic Soul and Mr Lincoln can track the pace prominently, while the majority are hold-up performers who will need the race to develop. The strong early pace should stretch the field and create a searching test. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers and horses with tactical speed, as the early burn will compromise pure hold-up horses who need to come from too far back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Trackers Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If Cosmic Soul or Mr Lincoln can track the pace without getting embroiled in early speed
scenarios.body: The genuine gallop will stretch the field and allow these tactical types to pick off the pace-setters in the final furlong. Their ability to be handy without leading makes them perfectly positioned when the front runners tire.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If Ailt An Chorrain or Scriabin can steal a march when the other folds
scenarios.body: One of the pace-setters gets first run on the field and holds on grimly up the hill. The good ground and 2m trip allows a bold front runner to see out the trip if they can break clear.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Charges
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is even stronger than expected and completely empties the leaders
scenarios.body: The genuine gallop sets up perfectly for a closer with a turn of foot to sweep past tired horses. King Sacre or Pure Gold could benefit if they get the right racing room and tactical ride.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the main contenders all compromise each other positionally or tactically
scenarios.body: A lesser-fancied runner like Largy Meadow gets an uncontested run through on the rails or finds a perfect pitch. The competitive handicap nature means any horse getting the right trip can cause an upset.

watchPoints.text: Cosmic Soul could be overbet given his hat-trick form but the 2m trip is minimum for this progressive stayer
Watch the pace battle between Ailt An Chorrain and Scriabin as both will want to lead and neither gives ground easily
King Sacre's finishing kick was impressive at Hexham but he needs the leaders to come back to him significantly
Pure Gold has been well beaten twice at this course since April and may be reaching her ceiling in the handicap
Scots Poet carries a 5lb penalty but has good course form and the good ground will suit his style perfectly

races.name: Perth Silver Cup Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Classic Maestro
runners_data.note: Leading runner with proven stamina who won gruelling 2m4f contest here in April, only 2lb higher today with strong recent form
runners_data.comment: Some positive runs this term but he may not have his favoured soft/heavy ground
runners_data.spotlight: Battled on well to win gruelling contest here (2m4f, good) in April; that form is treated with a degree of caution but he's only 2lb higher today and this shorter trip on forecast slower ground will suit.

runners_data.name: Itwasfate
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning after 305 days with concerning run-out last time, making reliability questionable despite higher class
runners_data.spotlight: Ex-Irish 9yo who is 1-5 in British points this year; ran out on latest appearance three weeks ago and it's hard to tell whether he can still be competitive off this sort of mark under rules.

runners_data.name: Newtown Rambler
runners_data.note: Front-runner wearing cheekpieces and tongue-tie who made all over course and distance last time, proven track specialist
runners_data.comment: Ex-Irish; hurdles winner in headgear for this yard in March; fair chase form; interesting
runners_data.spotlight: Bounced back to form with hurdle win in first-time cheekpieces/refitted tongue-tie in March, his second start for Adrian Keatley, and made all over C&D (good to soft) when back over fences last month; obvious contender.

runners_data.name: Garde Des Champs
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with modest strike-rate but consistent placings, offers tactical alternative in pace-dominated field
runners_data.comment: Not best of strike rates (both wins over C&D); not jump well here last time; bit to prove
runners_data.spotlight: Has modest strike-rate (2-41 under all codes) and was behind Newtown Rambler and Hypotenus when fourth of seven over C&D good to soft) last month but is now 1lb lower than for last summer's convincing C&D (good) win, and can't be ruled out.

runners_data.name: Captain Cool
runners_data.note: Leading runner in excellent form with recent chase wins, only five days since last run may raise stamina questions
runners_data.comment: Went 2-2 over fences at Plumpton week ago; back hurdling off 5lb lower mark so a player
runners_data.spotlight: Launched chasing career with wins at Stratford (2m1f, good to firm) and Plumpton (2m1f, good) last month, and also ran well when second over hurdles on Tuesday; evidently in very good nick but current chase mark asks a question of him, and today's forecast slower ground is probably not ideal.

runners_data.name: Hypotenus
runners_data.note: Free-going front-runner who struggled on debut for new trainer, needs to prove he can handle the pace pressure
runners_data.comment: Taunton chase win for Joe Tickle; wind op since; could bounce back from poor run last time
runners_data.spotlight: Free-goer who often makes the running; well beaten when last of three on debut for Neil Mulholland in April but last month's third of seven behind Newtown Rambler over C&D (good to soft) was more encouraging, and he may yet have more to offer for his new stable.

races.paceDynamic: Classic Maestro, Captain Cool, Newtown Rambler, and Hypotenus all possess prominent early speed, creating an inevitable strong gallop from the off. With four confirmed pace-setters in a six-runner field, the early fractions will be testing and stamina becomes paramount over the final half-mile. Only Garde Des Champs offers a hold-up alternative, but the sustained pace will suit horses who can travel strongly in the leading group without overexerting. This race shape strongly favours those with proven stamina reserves who can sustain their effort when the pace bites.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sustained Gallop Grind
scenarios.trigger: If all four pace-setters engage from the start and maintain a strong tempo throughout
scenarios.body: The relentless pace will find out the stamina-light runners, allowing the most robust stayer to prevail in a war of attrition. Classic Maestro and Newtown Rambler have both proven their staying power in gruelling contests at this track.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Early Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If Captain Cool or Hypotenus crack early, reducing the pace pressure significantly
scenarios.body: A more tactical affair develops where hold-up horses can conserve energy and deliver late challenges. Garde Des Champs benefits most from this scenario with his patient running style, while Newtown Rambler can time his challenge.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Captain Cool Dominance
scenarios.trigger: If Captain Cool's recent form progression continues and he can dictate terms from the front
scenarios.body: The improving six-year-old uses his current confidence to control the pace and kick clear when it matters. His recent chase wins show he's learning to settle better while maintaining his tactical speed advantage over this field.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Itwasfate Revival
scenarios.trigger: If the ex-Irish pointer rediscovers his best form after recent disappointments
scenarios.body: The class horse in the field finally shows his true ability and outstays the pace-setters in the closing stages. His higher RPR rating of 132 suggests he has untapped potential if connections have resolved his recent running-out issues.

watchPoints.text: Captain Cool may struggle with stamina demands having run just five days ago in demanding conditions
Itwasfate's reliability after running out last time - watch for early signs of reluctance or waywardness
Hypotenus and how he settles early, as his free-going nature could see him burn out in the pace battle
Classic Maestro's jumping under pressure given his aggressive front-running style over shorter trip today
Garde Des Champs getting into contention turning for home as the only hold-up horse with a tactical advantage

races.name: Perth Gold Cup Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: The Real Whacker
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning from 57 days off with questionable recent form over 12 months
runners_data.comment: Well handicapped on peak efforts but those past glories may now be too distant
runners_data.spotlight: Now well handicapped judged on peak efforts, but his form during the last 12 months lacks substance; pulled up in the Grand National last time on his return to fences.

runners_data.name: Light N Strike
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse best suited to good ground, returning from long break but showed promise last time
runners_data.spotlight: Back from 193 days off when a 16l fourth to Somespring Special at Newton Abbot (2m5f) and ran as though that race would bring him on; that was his best effort yet since leaving Emma Lavelle, for whom he was competitive off higher marks; trip/ground fine.

runners_data.name: Magna Sam
runners_data.note: Prominent runner carrying 5lb claimer, long absence of 167 days and hasn't recaptured best form recently
runners_data.spotlight: Won the Edinburgh National over an extended 3m7f at Musselburgh in 2023 and 2025 (both good to soft); has not recaptured his form in his last three races and now returns from further wind surgery; 6lb out of the weights.

runners_data.name: Riskintheground
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse requiring good ground conditions, in-form Skelton team with just 14 days since last run
runners_data.comment: It was never in much doubt at Haydock despite the neck margin; only up 4lb
runners_data.spotlight: Good ground is key to him, though good to soft is acceptable; after signs of a revival at the Cheltenham Festival he duly delivered in a competitive 2m4f handicap at Haydock, winning cosily despite narrow margin of victory; the 4lb rise seemed generous and when beaten at Uttoxeter he bumped into the talented Glengouly on a good day; all his best form is at shorter, so stamina would be the principal concern.

runners_data.name: Breizh River
runners_data.note: Prominent runner on career-best form with recent wins, ideally placed for early tactical position
runners_data.comment: Not as good as he was but has still won two of his last four races; raised 5lb for Kelso
runners_data.spotlight: Career bests on the RPR front in his last two races, winning at Kelso (2m5f) and close up at Aintree (2m4f; again on good); could run well, though a nagging concern that he didn't appear to stay 3m when he tried it once before (at this track).

runners_data.name: Statuario
runners_data.note: Prominent runner seeking hat-trick in this race with excellent course record and just 1lb penalty
runners_data.comment: Second in this race in 2025; two C&D wins on good since, latest in September; contender
runners_data.spotlight: Seeking a hat-trick in this race and on the back of a seventh course success in April when he dead-heated over this trip; not handicapped out of it after just a 3lb rise, for all that he's never defied this high a mark in the past.

runners_data.name: Somespring Special
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare with back-to-back recent wins on good ground, proven stamina over trip
runners_data.comment: Made it 5-16 over fences when scoring at Newton Abbot (2m5f); respected back up in trip
runners_data.spotlight: Has enhanced her good strike-rate over fences with back-to-back wins at Newton Abbot (2m5f) and Bangor (3m; again on good); it was harder work last time after a 6lb rise and she now has another 5lb to contend with, though last time was her first go over this far.

runners_data.name: Duffle Coat
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with poor recent record but previous big-race experience including Galway Plate second
runners_data.comment: No show on comeback run in Irish National; hard to be confident in although ground to suit
runners_data.spotlight: Only 1-20 over fences, the win coming in the 3m Mayo National in 2024 (good ground); finished a fine second in the Galway Plate that summer but he's been underperforming for a while now and belatedly tries a tongue-tie.

runners_data.name: Walk On Quest
runners_data.note: Prominent runner missing key jockey Jack Power, recent Kelso winner but tactical disadvantage
runners_data.comment: Won 4 handicaps 2 seasons ago; sound run when beaten a nose over C&D latest; contender
runners_data.spotlight: Made it 5-12 over fences when readily taking care of two rivals over a similar trip at Kelso a month ago (good; made most); only 3lb higher but without Jack Power's 5lb claim, so at this level he's probably in need of his best form yet.

runners_data.name: Stans The Man
runners_data.note: Lone pace-setter on hat-trick bid, 4lb lower than last year's third, perfectly positioned tactically
runners_data.comment: Won this in 2025 and returned to form at end of last season; high on the list
runners_data.spotlight: On a hat-trick when a fairly close third in this last year and he returns off a 4lb lower mark, and in a solid run of form; enters the reckoning.

races.paceDynamic: Stans The Man will set the pace without pressure, as the only confirmed front-runner in this 10-runner field. The Real Whacker, Magna Sam, Breizh River, Statuario and Walk On Quest will create significant congestion in prominent positions, leading to inevitable traffic problems turning for home. The three hold-up horses (Light N Strike, Riskintheground, Somespring Special, Duffle Coat) will have clear runs through but must overcome the tactical disadvantage of giving ground away over this extended trip. This pace setup strongly favours prominent runners who can secure good positions early and avoid the mid-race squeeze.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Pace Benefits
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely sustainable and the prominent group stays together
scenarios.body: The congested prominent runners get first run on the leader while hold-up horses face too much ground to make up over 3m. Those who secure the best early positions in the prominent pack will have decisive advantages.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent congestion creates significant interference 2-3 out as predicted
scenarios.body: The traffic problems allow patient hold-up horses with clear runs to sweep through late. Light N Strike and Somespring Special benefit most from their tactical positioning.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Leader Dominates Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Stans The Man gets an easy lead and the pace becomes too slow early
scenarios.body: The uncontested leader builds an unassailable advantage while the prominent group fails to organize an effective challenge. His hat-trick bid succeeds from the front.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes unsustainably fast due to prominent overcrowding
scenarios.body: Both leader and prominent horses fade badly, leaving the race to the most patient hold-up horses who conserved energy. The finish becomes a sprint between the back-markers.

watchPoints.text: Watch for severe traffic problems involving Breizh River, Walk On Quest and Statuario when the prominent group converges 2-3 furlongs out
Monitor if Stans The Man gets too easy a lead early as the prominent horses may be reluctant to engage
Light N Strike's fitness after 32-day break following 193-day absence could be crucial to hold-up chances
Observe if 5lb claimers Isabelle Ryder and James Smith can handle the tactical pressure on Magna Sam and Duffle Coat
Track whether the good ground maintains throughout as several key contenders specifically require these conditions

races.name: Malcolm Group Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Buy Some Time
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse switching from hurdles to chasing who needs the pace to be strong to be effective from the rear
runners_data.comment: Ex-pointer; won twice over 3m here in 2024; creditable third over 2m4f here latest; chance
runners_data.spotlight: Raced exclusively over hurdles since finishing second in Cartmel hunter chase on rules debut in spring 2024; caused 50-1 shock at 2025 Punchestown festival and has been placed twice in today's headgear combination here this spring (2m4f/3m2f); contender if able to transfer that form to fences.

runners_data.name: Inis Oirr
runners_data.note: Course and distance winner who stays well but needs strong tempo to show his best form from off the pace
runners_data.comment: Back to form with a C&D win last month but not sure to be in the same mood again
runners_data.spotlight: Generally disappointing since winning valuable marathon in February 2024 but won off much-reduced mark over C&D (good) in April and also ran well when second behind a progressive rival here last month; considered.

runners_data.name: Sir Carnegie
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with course form and first-time blinkers who may be positioned closer given recent tactical wins
runners_data.comment: Dug deep at Perth (2m4f; from 4lb lower) latest; blinkers newly applied & claimer ridden.
runners_data.spotlight: Placed twice over C&D before keeping on well to win three-finisher contest here (2m4f, good to soft) last month; fourth win over fences came with first-time blinkers (instead of cheekpieces) at Hexham (3m) yesterday evening when he got up close home; respected if he turns out quickly again.

runners_data.name: Settle Down Jill
runners_data.note: Strong recent hunter chase winner who races from the rear but carries career-high weight in this company
runners_data.comment: Fair form in hunter chases but held by Whatdeawant on last month's Hexham form
runners_data.spotlight: Looked in very good nick when readily winning Kelso hunter chase (2m7f, good) for his owner-trainer last month but faces quite daunting assignment off career-high mark on this return to a handicap; now in the care of Tristan Davidson.

runners_data.name: Ira Hayes
runners_data.note: Front-running leader who won last time when others fell, giving him tactical control but questions over true merit
runners_data.comment: Fortunate when winning last month but with respected stable and unexposed over fences
runners_data.spotlight: Almost certainly fortunate when winning Tramore beginners' chase (2m5f, good to yielding) in April, given he was in fourth (albeit close up) when the front three came to grief two out, but ran big race when clear second in Market Rasen handicap (3m, good) last month and features prominently in calculations here.

runners_data.name: Wasdell Dundalk
runners_data.note: Veteran course specialist returning from hurdles who has proven stamina but may lack the pace for this scenario
runners_data.comment: Solid record over fences here - four wins at 3m - which does at least offer some hope.
runners_data.spotlight: Veteran who gained four of his six chase wins over C&D and is versatile regarding ground; well beaten when 50-1 for 2m4f hurdle here last month, after a layoff, but that was also the case before he bounced back to form and finished second in this race a year ago; can't be ignored.

runners_data.name: Neon Diamond
runners_data.note: Prominent horse from strong stable who represents the main tactical threat to track the leader throughout
runners_data.comment: 1-7 over hurdles, beaten off 115 in first h'cap chase, may do better if rain arrives
runners_data.spotlight: Yet to make any further progress since easily winning Kilarney maiden hurdle (2m7f, yielding to soft) in first-time cheekpieces last summer and was well held when upped to 3m2f for handicap chase debut in April (her fourth run over fences); that said, her stable's runners are always respected here.

runners_data.name: Muskerry Rock
runners_data.note: Non-runner
runners_data.comment: Two wins in points last autumn, more recent form has been less encouraging
runners_data.spotlight: Dual point winner who came good under rules with front-running success in Wexford hunter chase (2m7f, good to yielding; refitted cheekpieces) last month; faces tougher opposition here, having recently changed hands for £17,000, but it will be interesting to see what Dan Skelton can do with him.

races.paceDynamic: Ira Hayes is the lone confirmed pace-setter and will dictate terms from the front without pressure in this small field. With six hold-up horses and only one prominent runner (Neon Diamond), Ira Hayes will control a steady gallop through the early stages before the race unfolds late. The lack of early pace will create a tactical affair where horses need to be positioned to strike, favouring those with tactical speed who can quicken when the race develops. This race shape strongly favours front-runners and horses with enough pace to track the leaders, disadvantaging pure hold-up horses who rely on a strong gallop.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Ira Hayes maintains control without serious challenge until late
scenarios.body: The modest pace allows him to conserve energy and kick clear when the hold-up horses are still being organized for their runs. His tactical advantage from controlling the tempo proves decisive over this stamina test.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Surge Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes genuinely slow and turns into a sprint finish
scenarios.body: The hold-up horses get their preferred scenario with a searching finish that plays to their closing kick. Quality rather than position determines the outcome in a bunched finish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Neon Diamond or another horse tracks Ira Hayes closely throughout
scenarios.body: The tracker can monitor the leader's every move and time their challenge perfectly in the straight. Being in the slipstream while staying out of trouble proves the winning formula.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Completely
scenarios.trigger: If Ira Hayes goes too slow and gets swamped by superior finishing speed
scenarios.body: The race becomes a messy scramble where class and recent form trump tactics. The horses with the strongest recent performances can overcome poor positioning.

watchPoints.text: Ira Hayes sets fractions that are too slow early, allowing hold-up horses to close rapidly in the straight
Sir Carnegie's first-time blinkers create a more aggressive ride that disrupts the expected pace scenario
Neon Diamond positions closer to Ira Hayes than expected, creating earlier pressure and a stronger gallop
Settle Down Jill carries career-high weight after a hunter chase win and may struggle with the ratings rise
Weather changes affecting the good going, as several runners have mixed form on different surfaces

races.name: IM Group Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Maillot Blanc
runners_data.note: Prominent runner faces traffic concerns but won this race last year and arrives in career-best form
runners_data.comment: 3m Perth winner last summer; sound placed runs on last two starts; very much in the mix
runners_data.spotlight: Won this race last term and better form this spring, all on good ground; dead-heated for first at Kelso (2m5f) last time, which has pushed him up 3lb to his highest mark since 2024 but he looks much more likely than most of these to give his running; should be thereabouts.

runners_data.name: Our Girl Sal
runners_data.note: Prominent style, 364 days off but won last start for new trainer Paul Robson
runners_data.spotlight: Got up on the line at Kelso (3m2f) in May 2025 on second start for Paul Robson, opening her rules account; made the running when well beaten behind Maillot Blanc in this race last year, however, and not seen since; has changed hands and now has first run for Adam Nichol, with a tongue-tie (tried twice in 2024) restored.

runners_data.name: Stiletto
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse perfectly positioned to benefit from expected pace scenario but needs major revival
runners_data.comment: 8yo who has been well held in last three runs and needs a major revival after wind surgery
runners_data.spotlight: Won three times (2m2f-3m) in June-September last year, off today's mark over C&D on last occasion; out of form on last four outings, however, and a major revival is needed on this second start after wind surgery; tongue-tie (last used in 2024) returns.

runners_data.name: Dalileo
runners_data.note: Patient hold-up style suits the pace setup, won this race in 2024 from similar mark
runners_data.comment: Three-time Perth winner (2m4f-3m); well beaten on Wednesday on first run since November
runners_data.spotlight: This race in 2024 is among his three Perth wins from 23 visits; latest win was last July over C&D again from 2lb higher than today and that was his second run after a break, the same scenario which presents itself today; needs a second look but others are preferred for the win.

runners_data.name: Burgundy Man
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner returns to hurdling after three poor chase runs this spring
runners_data.comment: C&D winner (chasing debut) last October; well beaten on both subsequent starts; risky.
runners_data.spotlight: 0-20 over hurdles but won here (3m, soft) on chase debut last October; three major backward steps this spring prompt caution on this return to hurdling, with cheekpieces (tried often as hurdler last year) reinstated.

runners_data.name: Shighness
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with 5lb claimer but unreliable and unseated last time
runners_data.comment: On a handy mark and back to some form on last hurdles start so hard to rule out.
runners_data.spotlight: No win since a chase early in 2024; only occasional echoes of that form and she was held when unseating on the turn at Hexham on latest start.

runners_data.name: Leader Wing
runners_data.note: Prominent runner, 79 days off but consistent record of minor honours over 3m
runners_data.comment: Effective over C&D; creditable third to Big Storm Brewing latest; hurdles score is 0-14
runners_data.spotlight: Won a bumper in May 2024; 0-15 as a hurdler for Gillian Boanas but had his share of seconds and thirds, including over 3m; £12,500 sale in March was quickly followed by wind surgery and, although usual headgear is dispensed with, new trainer Dan Skelton has something to work with; one to note.

runners_data.name: Jakana
runners_data.note: Prominent style, showed revival on chase debut here but failed at Cartmel subsequently
runners_data.comment: 12l fourth on last month's Perth chasing debut, shaping as if needing further than 3m.
runners_data.spotlight: Partial revival on chase debut here (3m, good) in April but she did not shine at Cartmel one month later; has plenty of form to make this look an attractive mark but there are doubts on this return to hurdling.

runners_data.name: Creadan Grace
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse from Gordon Elliott stable, won last time at 3m and suits patient tactics
runners_data.spotlight: Upped to 3m for a last-gasp win in 20-runner race at Down Royal in October; respectable fourth of 18 under James Smith at Punchestown (again 3m on good to yielding) last month confirms her in serious calculations.

runners_data.name: Reagrove Lord
runners_data.note: Prominent runner receiving 32lbs from top weight, first run for 400 days last time
runners_data.spotlight: 0-17 as hurdler but plenty of minor honours, including C&D; needs to improve upon last month's fourth at Hexham but that was his first run for 400 days, so he may well build on that; case can be made off career-low mark.

runners_data.name: Myfavouritesister
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with 3lb claimer, 13-race maiden but showed hurdle form last year
runners_data.comment: Consistent maiden hurdler; off since September but no forlorn hope now going chasing
runners_data.spotlight: 13-race maiden, with nine of those races over hurdles; did little on chase debut last time (after six months off) but several bits of hurdle form last year, including over C&D, give her a place chance.

runners_data.name: Luminaries
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer, 143 days off and inconsistent but has 3m winning form in spring months
runners_data.comment: Needs to get back on track but he's on a dangerous mark and is 3-3 over C&D
runners_data.spotlight: Tried chasing last autumn and did not show much back over hurdles in the winter on last two outings; 4-20 overall as a hurdler, with all four wins in March-May 2025, but there have to be questions at the moment.

runners_data.name: Watchoutitscookie
runners_data.note: Prominent runner getting 24lbs from top weight, consistent minor honours record
runners_data.comment: Inconsistent, but a leading player if reproducing his latest third at Exeter last month.
runners_data.spotlight: 2m4f hurdle and 2m7f chase winner (once each) from 35 races; his last win was in 2024 but bits of form this year, including penultimate start, give him an each-way chance.

runners_data.name: Breaking Ground
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse fades in finish, handicap debut over much longer trip with tongue-tie fitted
runners_data.comment: Signs of only a little ability and needs to find significant improvement in tongue-tie
runners_data.spotlight: This is her handicap debut and a major step up in trip, but there have been signs of only a little ability; tongue tied on latest start and a hood (tried four starts back, pulled up) is reinstated.

races.paceDynamic: Burgundy Man will lead with no early pressure in this 3m handicap hurdle, setting a comfortable gallop that should suit the prominent runners early. Six horses (Maillot Blanc, Our Girl Sal, Leader Wing, Jakana, Reagrove Lord, Watchoutitscookie) all want prominent positions, creating congestion and traffic problems turning for home. The sustainable early pace followed by late congestion strongly favours hold-up horses who can pick their way through and finish late. This race shape clearly benefits the patient, hold-up performers who avoid the mid-race squeeze.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Heroes Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If Burgundy Man sets steady fractions and the prominent brigade get tangled up 2-3 out
scenarios.body: The patient closers avoid trouble and pick off the tiring leaders in the final furlong. Stiletto and Dalileo benefit most from this tactical setup.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Escape Traffic
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent runners gets first run before the squeeze develops
scenarios.body: Maillot Blanc or Our Girl Sal break clear before the congestion hits and hold on grimly. Their superior class tells when they get racing room.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Burgundy Man Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If the leader's sustainable pace allows him to see off all challengers
scenarios.body: The front-runner's stamina proves superior over this extended trip despite his poor hurdle record. The chasers never get close enough to threaten.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Early
scenarios.trigger: If Burgundy Man goes too slow and gets swamped by the prominent pack
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint finish with the handiest horses benefiting from tactical speed. Form and class become secondary to position.

Monitor Burgundy Man's jumping returning to hurdles after three poor chase runs this spring
Stiletto needs major revival but Sean Bowen booking suggests connections expect improvement
Shighness carries 5lb claimer Joshua Thompson but unseated on turn last time at Hexham
